scenarioStory.history: G2P1 at 38 weeks gestation. Patient reports her water broke approximately 10 minutes ago with a large gush of clear fluid, immediately followed by a sensation of something protruding from the vagina and an urge to push. She is now on hands and knees per her husband's instruction after he saw a loop of umbilical cord at the vaginal opening. Contractions are strong and about 3 minutes apart.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 30-year-old G2P1 female at 38 weeks in the knee-chest position with a visible, pulsating loop of umbilical cord protruding from the vaginal opening. Strong contractions are ongoing. → Cord manually elevated off presenting part: Crew places a gloved hand into the vagina and gently lifts the fetal presenting part off the cord to relieve compression, assesses for cord pulsations, and wraps the exposed cord in moist sterile gauze. → Position optimized, rapid transport initiated: Crew maintains sustained manual elevation of the presenting part off the cord, positions the mother in extreme Trendelenburg or knee-chest with hips elevated, applies high-flow oxygen, and expedites transport with advance notification to the receiving facility.
